feedback.worked_solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the origin is 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

So, the equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=196$ represents a circle that is centered at the origin, with radius

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{2} & =196 \\ r & =\sqrt{196} \\ r & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we disregarded the negative solution for the radius since the radius of a circle must be positive.

Therefore, the center is $(0,0)$ and the radius is $r=14.$
